newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks plunge at open then rebound.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks plunge at open then rebound.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index opened sharply lower on Thursday amid confusion about the accuracy of the stock market's quotes.
HSI Services Ltd, which calculates the Hang Seng Index based on stock exchange figures, told Reuters it could not confirm the accuracy of quotes showing a 515-point plunge at the open.
At 1430 GMT, the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) said the Hang Seng Index was operating properly.
Based on traded prices in the first half hour, the index quickly pared the initial losses to trade 104 points down at 13,085.
"All trades were done at correct prices," said Anthony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas. "Only the historical information on the screen was wrong."
He added: "The problem only caused a small inconvenience at the open."
Brokers said the index was likely to seesaw at the 13,100 level due to greater investor caution prompted by new volatility in the market.
On Wednesday, the index swung quickly from 75 points up to more than 200 points down in afternoon trading, closing 152.86 points down at 13,189.60.
Technical analysts said a drop of more than 500 points at Thursday's open was not a surprise, given the volatility in overseas markets.
Wall Street's Dow Industrials ended 70.73 points down overnight at 6,402.52, after nervously dipping 130 points intraday.
"The short-term impact on Hong Kong is quite strong," said Ted Chen, technical analyst at Technical Data Inc. "The index found support at the 12,600 level and is now going back to 13,300."
He added that while the long-term trend is still up, the index was likely to establish a trading range between 12,800 and 13,200 in the near term.
Trading in Hang Seng Index futures was active despite the initial confusion over the calculation of the index.
"The problem was rectified shortly after the opening," said Kenneth Tang, director of Sassoon Securities.

Tang said the exchange had advised subscribers to its information service that the high and low shown at the bottom of news page 788 was correct, showing a low of 12,960.81 and indicating a fall of 228.79 points from Wednesday's close.
The December index futures contract was trading about 40 points down at 13,110.
